newsitem.title: ITALY: Another mob murder reported in southern Italy.
newsitem.headline: Another mob murder reported in southern Italy.

text.p: A man was shot dead in broad daylight as he strolled along the main boulevard of this south Italian city on Sunday in the latest incident of mob violence that has swept the area since the beginning of the year, Italian news agency Ansa reported.
Domenico Zippo's murder brings the death toll in the crime-ridden areas of Caserta and nearby Naples to 89 in the last six months.

About 500 troops have been deployed in and around Naples over the past week to help quell violence that has erupted as rival clans of the Camorra, the Naples Mafia, have waged street battles for supremacy.
But five people were killed in this past weekend alone, including a 17-year-old boy who was shot outside Naples by hitmen who were gunning for his friend, a suspected clan member.
On Saturday, suspected gangster Nicola Cirillo, who was wanted for robbery and extortion, was shot in the head while driving his car. Police said the murders of Cirillo and Zippo may be related.
Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano, who has visited Naples, admitted that fighting the Camorra would be an uphill battle.
"There is no magic wand that can halt this spiral of murders right away. But we have to continue with tenacity," Napolitano said in an interview with Italian daily La Repubblica on Sunday.
"At this moment, because of the aggressiveness and the continued attacks on citisens, the Camorra is perhaps more dangerous than the (Sicilian) Mafia."
About 80 clans of the Camorra, with several thousand affiliates, operate in and around Naples. Unlike their herarchical Sicilian counterparts, the Camorra is loosely organised.
